faults.note: The apparent-depth paragraph jumps from 'the sideways step each ray makes' to depth ÷ n without saying that the same sideways step is reached by the real ray going down at r and the traced-back line at i, so x = real × tan r = apparent × tan i. Screen 10 says the law 'would need a sine above 1' without showing why: sin r = 1.333 × sin i, which passes 1 once sin i passes 0.750.

'It cannot happen going into a slower material' holds: there sin r = (n1/n2) sin i is always smaller than sin i. 'Glass traps light more easily' holds for every common glass, each with an index above water's. The fibre warning is a safety rule, not a claim.
